title: Mouse intraductal modeling of primary ductal carcinoma in situ
protocol: Dissect resected sample with scalpels in a few mL of Digestion solution on a 6 cm petri dish.
Transfer tumor pieces to a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add 10 mL of digestion solution per 100 mg of tumor tissue.
Incubate the mixture in a shaker at 100 rpm at 37°C for 16 h overnight.
Transfer the contents to 15 mL falcon tubes and spin at 1500 × g for 10 min.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed Trypsin-EDTA and gently pipette up and down for 1 min at 20°C.
Add 9 mL of ADDF+++ and spin at 1500 × g for 10 min.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 9 μL of DNAse solution.
Vortex the mixture for 3-5 minutes.
Add 6 mL ADDF+++ and spin at 1500 × g for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL ADDF+++, coating the pipette with a 2.5% BSA solution by pipetting up and down twice.
Filter the solution through a 70 μm cell strainer (coated with 2.5% BSA) into a 50 mL falcon tube (coated with 2.5% BSA).
Transfer the filtered solution into a 15 mL falcon tube (coated with 2.5% BSA) and spin at 1500 × g for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and suspend the cells in 100 μL of PBS (use up to 1 mL of PBS if a large pellet is present).
Keep the cell suspension on ice from this point onwards.
Take 10 μL of the cell suspension and add 10 μL of trypan blue.
Pipette 10 μL of the mixture onto a cell counting chamber.
Count cells using a cell counter to determine the number of viable cells.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension needed to obtain 25,000 cells in 18 μL for intraductal injection.
Immobobilize and anesthetize the mouse.
Shave the area around the nipple carefully to make it visible.
Prepare the setup in a laminar flow hood.
Place 3 sterile diapers at the bottom of the cabinet.
Install a camera in the cabinet.
Install a screen in the cabinet.
Install a small heating pad in the cabinet.
Wipe everything that will be in contact with the mouse or you during surgery with disinfectant.

Introduce sterile materials into the biohazard cabinet: tissues, razor blades, 70% Ethanol, PBS, 15 mL Falcon tube, P20 pipet and tips, 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, anesthesia induction box, waste box, Evans blue (2 mg/mL), syringes, tweezers, Hamilton syringe.
Turn on heating pad at 37°C.
Connect a 5 mL syringe to the isoflurane station without plunger for use as a head cone during shaving and injection.
Anesthetize the mouse with 2.5% isoflurane and 2 L per minute air flow until it falls asleep.
Carefully shave around the nipples of the anesthetized mouse.
Place the mouse in the isoflurane/5 mL syringe on a heating pad under the camera.
Clean the Hamilton syringe with PBS before use.
Prepare droplets of 20 μL (2 μL Evans blue + 18 μL tumor cells) for injection.
Fill the syringe carefully to avoid air bubbles, which can clog mammary ducts.
Remove the cap of dead skin on the nipple with tweezers if present.
Hold the nipple between the tweezers.
Inject 20 μL cell suspension into the nipple.
Check if the solution disperses in the mammary gland.
Monitor outgrowth for primary DCIS samples, which typically takes 6–12 months to form lesions.
Sacrifice the animal.
Carefully dissect out the injected mammary glands.
Place the mammary gland in a 12- or 24-well plate.
Perform a mild digestion for 20–30 min at 37°C on a shaker (100 rpm) in 2 mL of mild digestion mix.
Wash the gland three times for 5 min in 2 mL HBSS at 20°C on a shaker (100 rpm).
Perform a 2-h fixation in 2 mL PLP at 20°C.
Wash the mammary glands twice in 2 mL NH4Cl (0.5 M) for 10 min.
Wash the gland three times for 10 min in 2 mL PBS at 20°C on a shaker.
Add 2 mL blocking buffer for 3 h at 20°C on a shaker.
Incubate with selected primary antibodies diluted in 2 mL blocking buffer overnight (±16 h) at 20°C on a shaker.
Wash samples three times for 10 min in 2 mL PBS with 0.2% Tween at 20°C on a shaker.
Incubate with secondary antibodies in 2 mL blocking buffer for at least 5 h, protected from light at 20°C on a shaker.
Wash for 30 min in 2 mL PBS with 0.2% Tween and DAPI (1 μg/mL) at 20°C on a shaker.
Wash three times for 20 min in 2 mL PBS with 0.2% Tween at 20°C on a shaker.
Mount the mammary gland between two coverslips using a whole-gland mounting device.
Image the tissue using a confocal microscope.
Sacrifice the animal and carefully dissect out the injected mammary glands.
Repeat steps 1 to 11, only suspend cells in 300 μl of cold PBS with 0.5% BSA at step 11.
Add 100 μL of human FcR Blocking Reagent for up to 108 total cells (20 μL of FcR per 60 μL buffer/ 107 cells).
Label cells with biotinylated antibodies (Mouse Anti-MHC Class I and II) at a dilution of 1:100 (for 400 μl PBS with 0.5% BSA and FcR add 4 μl antibodies).
Incubate for 20 min on ice.
Wash cells by adding 5–10 ml of PBS with 0.5% BSA per 107 cells and centrifuge at 1500 × g for 10 min.
Aspirate supernatant completely then repeat wash.
Resuspend pellet in 300 μL PBS with 0.5% BSA and add 100 μL of Anti biotin MicroBeads UltraPure.
Mix well and incubate for 20 min in the refrigerator at 2–8°C.
Wash cells by adding 5–10 mL of PBS with 0.5% BSA per 10^7 cells.
Centrifuge at 1500 × g for 10 min.
Resuspend up to 10^8 cells in 500 μL of PBS with 0.5% BSA.
Optional: Save 10 μL for pre-sort flow cytometry.
Place LD column in the magnetic field of a suitable MACS Separator.
Prepare LD column by rinsing with 2 mL of PBS with 0.5% BSA.
Discard effluent and change collection tube.
Apply cell suspension from step 44 onto the column.
Collect flow-through containing unlabeled human tumor cells.
Wash column with 2 mL of PBS with 0.5% BSA.
Collect unlabeled human tumor cells that pass through in the same collection tube as the previous step.
Remove column from the separator and place it on a new collection tube.
Pipette 2.5 mL of PBS with 0.5% BSA onto the column.
Immediately flush out the magnetically labeled cells by firmly pushing the plunger into the column.
Spin down the unlabeled cells from steps 48 and 49.
Resuspend the spun-down cells in 110 μL PBS.
Use 10 μL for counting as described previously in step 12.
Use another 10 μL for flow cytometry analysis.
Store the remaining cell suspension at 4°C for intraductal injection.
Label cells from step 52b with 1 μL of human specific EPCAM-e660 antibody (1:100).
Add 90 μL of cold FACS buffer and incubate for 20 min on ice covered with aluminum foil.
Wash the labeled cells by adding 5 mL of cold FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and suspend the cells in 500 μL of cold FACS buffer.
Add 5 μL of DAPI (1:100) to the suspended cells.
Perform flow cytometry analysis on these cells, the unstained cells from step 51 (control), and the pre-sort sample (optional).
Calculate the number of human tumor cells in the sample by combining the percentage of EPCAM positive cells and the number of cells counted in step 52a.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension needed to obtain 25,000 human cells in 18 μL.
Prepare the calculated volume of cell suspension for intraductal injection into each mammary gland.
Consider freezing excess single-cell solution for later use if more than 500,000 cells are available.
